title: WPPIL/155/2015 of Sadhu Ram Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (PIL) NO. 155 OF 2015
Sadhu Ram ..........Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. ......Respondents.
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Indu Sharma, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent
nos. 1 to 4.
Dated: 11.09.2015
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 Petitioner has approached this Court seeking the
following relief:
"I) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondents to conduct an
enquiry into the aforesaid allegations of public
importance having the public bearing affecting the public
rights at large."
2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
 There were allegations against the Pradhan of Village
Lakhnauta. The Authorities formulated charges. The District
Panchayat Raj Officer was the Inquiry Officer and he submitted a
report, as per which, out of 18 charges, 16 charges were proved. A
show cause notice was issued and a three-member Committee was
appointed to conduct the financial activities. The responsibility to
conduct the inquiry was vested with the District Development Officer,
i.e. the fifth respondent. The complaint is that the fifth respondent
mala fide, in the interest of the Pradhan, concluded the inquiry. There
was a direction of this Court in Writ Petition No. 641 of 2015 that the
inquiry be proceeded with. It is stated, by the order dated 18.05.2015,
that the financial power of the Pradhan was withdrawn. Petitioner
submitted a complaint before the District Magistrate as well as the

2
State Government to initiate de novo inquiry against seven set of
charges. The seven charges are mentioned in Paragraph 29 of the writ
petition, which are as follows:
"a) Fraudulent opening of accounts in the post office.
b) Disbursement of amount payable for toilets in the name
of dead persons.
c) Conducting meetings of the Panchayat by showing
fictitious presence of members to meet the quorum.
d) Utilizing the land lying in Khasra No. 318 recorded as
Johar for the purposes of construction of dwelling houses and
C.C. road.
e) Disbursing money under MANREGA for leveling of a
land in relation to a tenure holder who has no holding in the
village, and
f) Mis-utilization of money in the mud work of Rasta from
Chikitsalaya to Palla Ka Khet Shamshan tak."

3. The District Magistrate, taking cognizance to the
complaint, directed the District Development Officer to conduct
inquiry. The District Development Officer, pursuant to the direction
of the District Magistrate, conducted the inquiry and he finding that
one charge proved and in regard to other charges, there is no material,
submitted the inquiry report. It is an admitted case that the Pradhan
has been removed pursuant to the inquiry report. It is feeling
aggrieved by the District Development Officer's finding and praying
that an inquiry may be conducted fairly by any authority including the
District Magistrate, that the petitioner is before us.
4. We heard the learned senior counsel for the petitioner
and the learned Deputy Advocate General.
5. From the nature of the case, we are of the view that we
need not entertain this writ petition in public interest jurisdiction. It is
a case, where the Pradhan has already been removed by the fifth
respondent. As far as the charges are concerned, no doubt the
petitioner has a case that there are materials and the inquiry conducted
by the District Development Officer is not proper. We would think
that the petitioner must seek remedies elsewhere in a competent
forum. We need not entertain this writ petition. Without prejudice to

3
the rights of the petitioner to bring the lacunae or illegality into the
notice of the competent body, which the learned Deputy Advocate
General would point out the power is there with the State
Government, the writ petition is closed.
